newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end at third straight record close.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end at third straight record close.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended at record highs for a third straight session on Wednesday after a huge deal involving Laidlaw Inc offset modest profit-taking in other sectors.
The TSE 300 Composite Index edged up 3.31 points to finish at 5271.79, surpassing the previous record close set on Tuesday.
Trading was brisk with 90.2 million shares exchanging hands for a total value of C$1.17 billion ($853 million).
Advancing stocks outnumbered declines 468 to 442 with 287 issues unchanged. Toronto's 14 sub-groups were evenly split with gains led by a 343-point surge in transportation.
Laidlaw Inc was the session's heaviest trader after it announced plans to sell its solid waste unit to Arizona-based Allied Waste Industries for US$1.5 billion.
On the weak side, some investors took profits in the wake of Toronto's recent record gains, stock analysts said.
Speculation that the U.S. Federal Reserve may raise interest rates at its September 24 policy meeting also unnerved investors.

"We're doing a balancing act. Last week everybody was excited because there appeared to be no inflation, but this week they think the Fed may bump rates," said Montreal-based technical analyst Bill Ram.

* Laidlaw class B topped the most-active list, rising 1.25 to 15.55 on 8.4 million shares. Laidlaw's class A shares climbed 1.35 to 15.50 on 304,000 shares. Analysts said Laidlaw may use some of the cash from the Allied deal to expand its remaining transport and waste businesses.

* Takeover target Loewen Group fell 0.45 to 54.50 on 613,000 shares in the wake of Monday's US$4.1 billion offer from Service Corp International. Loewen is expected to fight the suprise hostile bid from its industry rival.
Canada's other major funeral home operator, Arbor Memorial Services Inc, received a boost from the Loewen bid.
Arbor Memorial class A led net gainers, rising 1.50 to 25 in light volume.
* Goldstake Explorations Inc retreated 0.80 to 2.75 after climbing sharply Tuesday on encouraging assay results.
* Bombardier Inc class B fell 0.20 to 17.80 on 3.9 million shares, after losing 0.75 on Tuesday.

Dunnery Best of Richardson Greenshields of Canada Ltd said the freefall is due to market concerns about the fading popularity of the jet ski which has been a major contributor to Bombardier's bottom line.
